title: Does one evidence root correspond to one underlying observation?
frozenBefore: any corpus item was selected, any identity was computed, and any label was assigned under this rule
whyFrozenFirst: The quantity under test is a ratio between two counts, one of which (labelled observations) is produced by human judgement. A labelling rule written after seeing the root identities is a rule chosen knowing what ratio it produces. Freezing first, and blinding labellers to the identities, is the only thing separating this from an exercise that returns whatever number is wanted.

question.plain: When five issuers report the same event, does the aggregator see one root or five?
question.formal: For each proposition p, let R(p) be the number of distinct mp-root-v1 identities among parentless claims asserting p, and O(p) the number of distinct underlying observations those claims rest on, established by blinded labelling. Estimate the distribution of R(p)/O(p).
question.whyNotAnswerable: No theorem settles this. Every theorem in formal/lean/ is correct GIVEN the identity criterion; the criterion is an input, not a conclusion. mp-root-v1 (provenance/ROOT-IDENTITY.md) makes identity unforgeable, which is a different property from making it correspond to an observation. Issuer is part of the digest, so two issuers reporting one event produce two identities by construction.

population.frame: published claims about factual propositions that have since resolved, where each claim carries an authenticated issuer, a proposition identifier, an asserted value and an evidence reference sufficient to compute mp-root-v1
population.selection: the frame, the source set and the proposition list are declared at collection start and recorded in the manifest; neither is extended, narrowed or re-sampled after any identity is computed or any label is assigned
population.why: Below three claims a proposition cannot exhibit a split. Two hundred propositions is the smallest frame that can distinguish a median split factor of 1.0 from 1.5 at the spread seen in constructed cases; it is registered here rather than chosen later from the observed variance.
exclusions: propositions whose claims all originate from one issuer -- no split is possible and they only dilute the estimate
claims whose evidence reference is absent, since mp-root-v1 is not computable and the item is neither a split nor a merge but a missing input
population.exclusionsAreDeclaredNotDiscovered: both exclusions are properties of the record, decidable before any label exists

identityArm.definition: SHA-256 over authenticated issuer, issuer-scoped observation identifier, proposition, asserted value and evidence digest, per provenance/ROOT-IDENTITY.md
identityArm.computedBy: the shipped implementation, not a reimplementation, so the number measured is the number the system would act on
identityArm.blinding: identities are computed and sealed before labelling begins and are not visible to labellers

observationArm.unit: an underlying observation event -- the act of witnessing, not the act of reporting
observationArm.rule: two claims rest on the same observation if a labeller, seeing only the claim texts, their cited sources and their timestamps, judges that neither could have been produced without the other's source or a common source they both cite
observationArm.independence: labellers work independently, do not see each other's labels, and do not see any mp-root-v1 identity, issuer digest or root count

interRaterThreshold.statistic: Krippendorff alpha on the same-observation partition
interRaterThreshold.why: Below this the partition is not reproducible and the denominator of the ratio is noise. 0.67 is the conventional floor for tentative conclusions and is registered now so it cannot be relaxed to rescue a run.
interRaterThreshold.onFailure: the run STOPS and reports that the ground truth was not establishable on this corpus. It is not retried on a different corpus chosen because it agrees better; a second corpus, if any, is a new registration.

observationArm.adjudication: disagreements are resolved by majority of the three labellers; items with no majority are reported as unresolved and counted in a declared sensitivity band, not silently dropped

endpoint.primary: median split factor, median over propositions of R(p)/O(p)
endpoint.H0: median split factor = 1.0 -- root identity tracks observation identity
secondary: merge rate: proportion of labelled observation pairs judged distinct that share one mp-root-v1 identity
split factor distribution, not only its median, since a long tail matters even at a benign median
endpoint.bothDirectionsMatter: Split inflates margin and overstates security. Merge destroys margin and causes false abstention. They are different failures with different owners and are reported separately, never netted.

effectRequires.property: the measure can detect a split at all
effectRequires.rule: on constructed cases where the number of underlying observations is known by construction, the computed split factor must recover the constructed value exactly
effectRequires.why: If mp-root-v1 collapsed everything to one identity, the real run would return 1.0 for a reason that has nothing to do with reporting behaviour. This is a sensitivity check on the instrument, run before the corpus, and it is not a result.
effectRequires.onFailure: the instrument is wrong and the real run does not start

effectRequires.property: the corpus can exhibit a split
effectRequires.rule: at least 20% of propositions must carry claims from three or more distinct issuers
effectRequires.why: A corpus where issuers rarely overlap cannot distinguish the hypotheses, however sound the method. Registered as a precondition rather than discovered as an excuse.

stopRule: collection ends at the declared proposition list, at the inter-rater failure condition, or at the instrument-sensitivity failure, whichever is first. The list is not extended and the labelling rule is not amended to obtain a result.

decisionRule.ifMedianSplitFactorAtOrBelow1_2: flip_budget may be described as an operational security budget, with the measured factor and its confidence interval disclosed alongside.
decisionRule.ifMedianSplitFactorAbove1_2: flip_budget must not be published as an operational security budget without dividing by the measured factor and disclosing the divisor. formal/CLAIM-SCOPE.md and PROVENANCE-REQUIREMENTS.md R3 are amended in the same change.
decisionRule.ifRunStops: the first gate in HRI-1 stands unchanged: flip_budget remains publishable as a count of root-set units, which is what it provably is, and not as a security budget.
decisionRule.why: The consequence is registered before the number exists so that an inconvenient result cannot be re-described as a limitation of the corpus.

whatThisDoesNotMeasure: whether any observation is true -- this is an independence measure, not an accuracy measure
deliberate identity splitting by one controller, which is HVI-1's question and has a different remedy
whether a production deployment uses RootRegistry at all, which is a deployment property recorded as LEDGER-H2 deployment_status
priorWork: None. This quantity has not been measured. formal/EXTENSION-SOCKETS.md section 5 identified it as the socket where a measurement, not a theorem, is what is missing; formal/THEOREM-LEDGER.json carries it as U1 underspecified.
